drivingQuestion: How to read Beit Shammai's 'she waits until majority, refuses and marries'?
outcomeNote: Shmuel's reading is left difficult (קשיא) against the mishna's wording.

segments.he: עוּלָּא אָמַר, תַּרְתֵּי קָתָנֵי: אוֹ שֶׁתְּמָאֵן וְתַגְדִּיל וְתֵיאָרֵס, אוֹ שֶׁתְּמָאֵן וְתִנָּשֵׂא לְאַלְתַּר.
segments.en: «Ulla said: Two» different possibilities «are taught» in Beit Shammai’s statement: «Either she should refuse, and» then once she «has matured» she «should become betrothed; or she should refuse and marry immediately.» She should not refuse and then only become betrothed again. According to Beit Shammai, as a minor, she may not refuse again.

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא עוּלָּא, הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי ״עַד שֶׁתַּגְדִּיל וְתִנָּשֵׂא״. אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל ״עַד שֶׁתַּגְדִּיל וְתֹאמַר״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! קַשְׁיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «Granted,» the explanation of «Ulla is» consistent with «that which is taught: Until she reaches majority and marries.» That is: Until she reaches majority, or until she marries. «But according to» the explanation of «Shmuel,» the mishna «should have» said: «Until she reaches majority and says» that she wishes to uphold the refusal. The Gemara comments: This phrase is «difficult» according to his explanation.
